propositions: The byte-equivalence oracle invokes a second copied Pandoc subprocess for each of 884 prepared corpus units, which shares mutable production constants with the real conversion and thus fails to independently validate byte output

Immutable golden output fixtures with deterministic regeneration and platform-keyed Pandoc version/binary fingerprint metadata can replace the coupled legacy subprocess while preserving all 884 real production Pandoc calls and cross-validation of format mutations

Single-platform binary SHA-256 schema caused CI failures on unsupported platforms; schema v2 retains generating platform plus complete darwin-arm64/linux-x86_64 fingerprint map with rejection of version/hash mismatches and unknown platforms

Paired local runtime measurement showed 32.3766s elapsed savings (49.4% reduction) and elimination of 884 duplicate Pandoc subprocesses while maintaining deterministic regeneration and all hardening test coverage
